doc.title: Carter Benny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: News of American swing reaching Europe
summary: Carter heard records and knew of Goodman's success, but felt little had developed in the meantime.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: While you were in Europe, how much news of musical developments in the U.S. was reaching you? Were you hearing latest recordings? After all, the swing era, which you had helped lay the foundation for, was now flourishing. How much news did you get of that?

Well, we were hearing records that were getting there; I don’t know how much later than having been released in America, but that’s about it, you know. It wasn’t . . . as a matter of fact, during that particular period, I don’t think there was too much, actually, too much development, as you call it. It was just going along sort of as I had left it.
Well I believe the Benny Goodman phenomenon had begun to take off . . .
. . . and that sort of thing. A lot of bands were being formed.
Oh yes, we were aware of that.
